metadata.title: [FEATURE]: Register A2A agents as tools using Agent Card metadata
metadata.author: KaRtHiK-56

description: # [FEATURE]: Support A2A Agent Card based registration when adding an A2A agent as a tool ## Summary The current "Add New A2A Agent" flow captures only a small subset of A2A metadata: Agent Name, Endpoint URL, Agent Type, Authentication Type, Description, Tags, Visibility, and Passthrough Headers. For A2A agents, this is limiting because the protocol defines an Agent Card as the standard discovery document for describing an agent’s identity, interfaces, capabilities, security requirements, skills, and related metadata. I’d like to add support for registering an A2A agent as a tool using its Agent Card, instead of treating it like a mostly generic endpoint. The current UI is shown in Figure 1 below. *Figure 1: Current A2A agent registration page with only basic endpoint and auth fields.* ## Problem A2A servers are expected to expose an Agent Card, and clients use it to discover capabilities and configure interactions correctly. The Agent Card includes metadata such as name, description, supported interfaces, provider, version, documentation URL, capabilities, security schemes, default input/output modes, skills, signatures, and icon URL. Right now, the registration form does not appear to provide a way to: - discover or fetch an Agent Card from the well-known A2A location, - capture supported interfaces including protocol binding and protocol version, - represent A2A capabilities such as streaming, push notifications, and extended agent cards, - represent agent skills in a structured way, - capture security schemes and security requirements beyond a simple auth type selector, - fetch or expose the authenticated extended agent card when supported. Because of this, an A2A agent can be registered, but a lot of A2A-specific semantics are either lost or need to be manually duplicated. ## Proposed enhancement Add an Agent Card-aware registration flow for A2A agents. ### Suggested behavior - Allow the user to register an A2A agent by providing either: - an A2A base endpoint, or - a direct Agent Card URL. - Attempt discovery via the standard well-known Agent Card location where applicable. - Fetch and parse the public Agent Card. - Pre-populate the form from the Agent Card instead of requiring manual entry for everything. - If the card declares `capabilities.extendedAgentCard = true`, allow authenticated retrieval of the extended Agent Card and merge or display the additional metadata. - Preserve manual override for fields that users may still want to edit locally. ### Suggested fields to surface from Agent Card At minimum, support storing and/or displaying: - `name` - `description` - `supportedInterfaces[]` including `url`, `protocolBinding`, `protocolVersion`, and optional `tenant` - `provider.organization` and `provider.url` - `version` - `documentationUrl` - `iconUrl` - `capabilities.streaming` - `capabilities.pushNotifications` - `capabilities.extendedAgentCard` - `capabilities.extensions[]` - `securitySchemes` - `securityRequirements` - `defaultInputModes` - `defaultOutputModes` - `skills[]` including `id`, `name`, `description`, `tags`, `examples`, `inputModes`, `outputModes`, and skill-level security requirements - `signatures` if present ## Why this matters This would make A2A agent registration more compliant with the protocol and reduce manual setup errors. It would also let the platform reason about what the agent actually supports, such as streaming, push notifications, or extended card retrieval, instead of inferring behavior from a generic form. There is already active A2A-related work in this repo, including recent issues and fixes around A2A listing and validation, so this would build on an area that is already evolving. ## Acceptance criteria - User can register an A2A agent from an Agent Card URL or discover it from the standard well-known location. - Registration flow parses and stores the public Agent Card fields listed above. - UI clearly shows supported interfaces, capabilities, skills, and security requirements for the registered agent. - If extended agent card support is declared, the UI allows authenticated retrieval and display of the extended card. - Manual overrides remain possible for editable local metadata. - Existing basic registration flow continues to work for non-A2A or partially compliant endpoints. ## Nice to have - Validate the selected interface and protocol version before saving. - Show protocol-derived warnings when the card declares unsupported optional capabilities. - Support card refresh/re-sync when the remote Agent Card changes, potentially using cache headers such as ETag / Cache-Control.
